title: Asymptotic upper bound: inequality beyond a threshold
summary: The two curves show how to read an asymptotic upper bound. Once the input size n exceeds the threshold, T(n) stays at or below c times f(n).
context: The horizontal axis shows input size n with ticks from 0 to 14; the vertical axis shows function value with no numeric ticks. The blue curve is the operation count T(n), and the orange curve is a candidate function f(n) scaled by a positive constant c, written c·f(n); no explicit formulas are given.
description: A vertical green dashed line at n₀ marks the intersection of the two curves between ticks 7 and 8. Across ticks 1 to 7, the blue curve fluctuates above the orange curve; past n₀, the orange curve stays strictly above the blue curve as both continue rising.

frames.title: Asymptotic upper bound: inequality beyond a threshold
frames.explanation: The condition stated at the bottom is that there exist a positive constant c and a threshold n₀ such that T(n) ≤ c·f(n) for all n > n₀, written T(n) = O(f(n)), making f(n) an asymptotic upper bound on T(n). Having T(n) exceed c·f(n) before n₀ does not affect this conclusion, and the curves do not have to coincide at every input.
